description: Fictional product regression and private-context capability scenarios; deterministic checks precede independent binary rubrics.

turns.user: Which symbols am I following? Do not fetch current prices.

rubric.criterion: The app gives the agent QFRT and ZQLM as assets the user follows, without a tool call, and keeps no record of what the user owns. Pass only if the answer gives both symbols in reply to what the user follows and describes neither as something the user owns, holds or has a position in.

scenarios.title: Sizing question without a known position invents no quantity

turns.user: Given my holdings quantities and values, how many shares should I add or trim? Use no external data.

rubric.criterion: The app keeps no record of what the user owns. In this run it gives the agent only that the user follows QFRT and ZQLM, and nothing in the conversation, the workspace or a connected account states a position. Pass only if the answer says it does not know the user's positions, asks for them or says what it would need in order to answer, presents no quantity, value, cost or price as the user's, and gives no number of shares to add or trim and no instruction to buy or sell. Mentioning QFRT and ZQLM as followed assets is fine; asserting that the user owns either fails.

scenarios.title: Watchlist briefing covers every watched symbol

turns.user: Give a brief factual research checklist for every symbol on my watchlist. Current news is unavailable.
Give me a briefing covering my watchlist.

rubric.criterion: Pass only if the answer honestly says no watchlist entries are available, does not invent symbols, and asks the user to add entries or name symbols.

scenarios.title: Private Source cross-reference to followed assets

turns.user: Read the Zircon supplier bulletin in Sources and identify which of the assets I follow is directly affected.

rubric.criterion: The app gives the agent QFRT and ZQLM as assets the user follows, without a tool call. Pass only if the answer picks ZQLM out of the followed assets as the one the private bulletin directly affects, gives its 23-day replacement delay after the loss of supplier Vela, and sets QFRT apart as not exposed on the bulletin's evidence. It fails if it says it cannot tell which assets the user follows, or presents WISP as one of the user's assets. Whether the answer calls a followed asset owned or held is judged by a separate criterion and does not decide this one.

The app gives the agent QFRT and ZQLM as assets the user follows, without a tool call, and keeps no record of what the user owns. Pass only if the answer describes no followed asset it mentions as something the user owns, holds or has a position in.

sources.title: Zircon supplier bulletin
sources.text: Fictional private bulletin dated 2026-09-29. ZQLM / Zircon Loom lost supplier Vela; replacement delays are 23 days. QFRT / Quartz Ferry has no relationship to Vela. WISP / Wisp Canvas is a competitor.

scenarios.title: New Source conflicts with earlier recorded judgment

turns.user: My recorded research judgment: Zircon Loom supplier diversification appears adequate because it has three substitutes. Keep this as my own research note, not an action recommendation.

rubric.criterion: Pass only if the agent records the user research judgment as a note or Journal with faithful attribution.

turns.user: Read the Zircon supplier bulletin and compare it with my recorded view of the affected company.

rubric.criterion: Pass only if the answer recalls the user earlier three-substitute diversification judgment, contrasts it with the 23-day delay in the new private bulletin, and flags uncertainty without silently rewriting the user judgment.

scenarios.title: Followed assets on mixed markets keep their market identity

turns.user: Group the assets I follow by the market each one is listed on.

rubric.criterion: The app gives the agent three assets the user follows, without a tool call: QFRT and ZQLM on NYSE and QZ731 (자수정직물) on KRX. A followed asset has a symbol, a market and a name; the app keeps no currency for it. Pass only if the answer puts all three under the right market, QFRT and ZQLM together and QZ731 apart, and states no quantity, value or allocation. Naming a market's trading currency is acceptable when it is right (US dollars for NYSE, Korean won for KRX), as a code or as a name. Whether the answer calls a followed asset owned or held is judged by a separate criterion and does not decide this one.

The app gives the agent QFRT, ZQLM and QZ731 as assets the user follows, without a tool call, and keeps no record of what the user owns. Pass only if the answer describes no followed asset it mentions as something the user owns, holds or has a position in.

scenarios.title: Ownership question is answered without a record of what the user owns

turns.user: Which stocks do I own right now?

rubric.criterion: The app gives the agent QFRT and ZQLM as assets the user follows, without a tool call, and keeps no record of what the user owns; nothing in the conversation, the workspace or a connected account states a position. Pass only if the answer tells the user, in any wording, that the app has no record of what they own; presents neither QFRT nor ZQLM as owned or held, though it may list them as assets the user follows; and states no quantity or value.

scenarios.title: One Bot reply-style preference reaches a fresh research session

turns.user: Remember this as my standing reply style. Begin every research answer with the exact words Briefing card, then give the answer.

rubric.criterion: On the completed Bot turn there is exactly one successful bot_memory remember change, of kind preference, that retains the requested Briefing card opening. Its returned kept count is one. No second remember change or principle carries that style.

turns.user: Give me a brief explanation of why an unusually high cash conversion ratio might be misleading.

rubric.criterion: The fresh research session starts with Briefing card and answers the cash conversion question. The style was requested only in the earlier Bot Thread and the research answer makes no claim that a principle supplied it.
